newsitem.title: TURKEY: Germany's Kinkel says no Europeans bow to Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kinkel says no Europeans bow to Turkey.

text.p: Visiting German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel on Wednesday hit back at Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan for a perceived slight on the European Union.
"No European will have to bow their head to Turkey in shame," Kinkel told German reporters on the first day of an official visit to Turkey.
The German delegation arrived in Turkey two hours late on Tuesday night after Kinkel delayed his departure from Rome to check comments by Erbakan, secular Turkey's first Islamist prime minister.

The entourage travelling with the foreign minister said he had come close to calling off the trip because of media reports quoting Erbakan as saying Kinkel should come to Turkey with his head hung in shame.

Erbakan told MPs of his Welfare Party on Tuesday that Turkey should be treated with more respect internationally. He said Ankara had incurred losses because of a customs accord with the EU that went into effect at the start of 1996.

"There will be a $5 billion loss for Turkey because it has entered the customs union ... After they have done this they will bow their heads when they talk with Turkey," Erbakan said. EU exports to Turkey have surged under the accord, while Turkish exports to the bloc have changed little.
